title: Who Owns the Building: Black Businesses, Rent and Commercial Property | At The Margins, Ep. 7
lede: Black households own about 2% of U.S. nonresidential commercial real estate wealth, compared with about 6% of owner-occupied homes (Brookings, from the Fed's 2019 SCF). Episode 7 of At The Margins follows the rent: who owns commercial property, how property in majority-Black ZIP codes is discounted, what tenants carry, community efforts to buy back the block, Toronto's Little Jamaica after 14 years of LRT construction, and what the evidence says about protecting businesses.
keyPoints: 3% of Black households own nonresidential commercial real estate vs 8% of white households; Black households hold ~2% of its value (Brookings, 2019 SCF).
11% of Black families own a business vs 16% of white families (Federal Reserve, 2022 SCF): the larger gap is in the buildings.
Retail property in majority-Black ZIP codes is undervalued by an estimated $171B, about $1.7M per building (Brookings estimate).
Little Jamaica: Crosstown construction began Nov 2011 and the line opened Feb 8, 2026; dozens of Black-owned businesses closed (CTV News).
Along Minnesota's Green Line, single-location business sales fell 10–20%, mostly after opening; mitigation ended with construction (University of Minnesota).
